messages.subject: Re: PX-DA sampling method
parts:
Hello Marc

Thank you for the references. I've skimmed them. They are mainly concerned with answering the question of identifying "big N"; i.e. the number of species at a site. I am more concerned with attempting to reduce potential autocorrelations in mcmc chains. i.e. There is body or work that does this sort of thing. The aim is to make the chains mix quicker. 

A simple example is the probit regression model. Depending on the actual model the autocorrelations can be very large! The PX-DA technique reduces the level of autocorrelations and ensure better mixing of MCMC chains.


See the code below:

#Some data simulated
set.seed(1)
n<-100
x<-scale(rnorm(n), T,T) #scaled and standardi
intercept<-0
beta<-5
e<-rnorm(n, sd=1)
z<- intercept + beta*x + e

y<- rep(1, n) 
y[which(z<0)]<-0


#The Bugs code
model<-
     "model
{    
     beta0 ~ dnorm(0, 1e-3)
     beta1 ~ dnorm(0, 1e-3)
     
     #likelihood part
     for (i in 1:n) #loop over each site
     {
          y[i]~dbern(p[i])
          p[i]<-phi(beta0+beta1*x[i])
     }#end of likelihood
}"



require(jagsUI)

#inputs for the Bayesian method
niter <- 50000
nburn <- 20000
nthin <- 1
nchains <- 3
nkeep<-(niter-nburn)*nchains


Data <- list(x=x, y=y, n=100)     
inits <- function(){list("beta0"=rnorm(1),"beta1"=rnorm(1))}

inits1=inits(); inits2=inits(); inits3=inits()
Inits=list(inits1,inits2,inits3)

# Paramaters to be monitored       
parameters <- c("beta0", "beta1") 
 
     
Runs <- jags(data=Data, inits=Inits, parameters.to.save=parameters, 
                  model.file=textConnection(model),
                  n.iter = niter, n.burnin = nburn, n.thin = nthin, 
                  n.chains = nchains, DIC = FALSE, verbose=FALSE) 


par(mfrow=c(1,2))
acf(Runs$sims.list$beta0,  main=expression(beta[0]), lag.max=250)
acf(Runs$sims.list$beta1,  main=expression(beta[1]),lag.max=250)





Regards
